subject: Error when I trying  to assess evolutionary allometry with procD.pgls

messages.author: e511f911cbbb2bd0
messages.subject: Error when I trying  to assess evolutionary allometry with procD.pgls
parts:
Hi folks,
Currently I am testing my landmarks based dataset with some analysis to explore size and species on shape for a  that contain 6 species. For this dataset I recently got the phylogenetic tree.
In previous analysis I ran the homogeneity of slopes test (HOS) with different options of the procD.lm function. As a result I obtained that the model that better describe the allometry was: coords ~ log(Csize)*species,  indicating that least one species displays a different allometry slope. If my interpretation are correct.

Recently I got a phylogenetic tree the genus, so now I'm trying to assess the allometry including this tree with procD.pgls.  Below my codes where I obtained not significant results when I test  pgls with the formula: coords ~ log(Csize). However, I get a Error message when I included interaction log(Csize):species.

Thanks in advance for any insight or advise about how can I fix this error.



# data preparation
mand_mand <- gpagen(mandible , curves= NULL)
mand_sub <- coords.subset(A= gpa_mand$coords, group = classifier_mand$species)
mand_mean <-lapply(mand_sub, mshape)
mand_mean <- simplify2array(mand_mean, higher = TRUE)
gpa_mean <- gpagen(mand_mean, curves= NULL)
species_mand <- unique(factor(classifier_mand$species))
gdf_mand_mean <- geomorph.data.frame(gpa_mean,
                                    species = species_mand,
                                    phy= tree)
#PGLS

simple_pgls <- procD.pgls(coords ~ log(Csize), phy = tree,
                       data = gdf_mand_mean, print.progress = FALSE)
#OUTPUT
           Df      SS       MS     Rsq      F       Z Pr(>F)
log(Csize)  1 0.00639 0.006392 0.01159 0.0469 -1.1006  0.834
Residuals   4 0.54516 0.136291 0.98841                      
Total       5 0.55156


# PGLS including interaction size*species
complex_pgls <- procD.pgls(coords ~ log(Csize)*species , phy = tree,
                       data = gdf_mand_mean, print.progress = FALSE)

# ERROR Message
 Error in (function (cond)  :
  error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 'as.matrix': subscript out of bounds

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Error when I trying  to assess evolutionary allometry with procD.pgls
parts:
Dear Julio,

There could probably be a better error message (we would have to catch this and have an error message that better explains why the error occurred) but the issue is caused by the invariance you create by holding constant the effect of phylogeny (species) and then having species as a term in your model.  I could replicate your issue with the plethspecies data.  I get the same error when attempting to do what you did:

> df = geomorph.data.frame(GPA, phy = plethspecies$phy, species = factor(dimnames(plethspecies$land)[[3]]))
> procD.pgls(coords ~ log(Csize) * species, data = df, phy = phy)

Error in (function (cond)  : 
  error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 'as.matrix': subscript out of bounds

I was able to produce a result by using just the interaction:

> anova(procD.pgls(coords ~ log(Csize):species, data = df, phy = phy))

Sums of Squares calculations: 1000 permutations.
  |==================================================================================| 100%

Analysis of Variance, using Residual Randomization
Permutation procedure: Randomization of null model residuals 
Number of permutations: 1000 
Estimation method: Generalized Least-Squares (via OLS projection) 
Sums of Squares and Cross-products: Type I 
Effect sizes (Z) based on F distributions
Df       SS   MS Rsq  F   Z Pr(>F)

log(Csize):species  8 0.043302    0   1  0 NaN  0.567
Residuals           0 0.000000 -Inf   0              
Total               8 0.043302                       

Call: procD.lm(f1 = coords ~ log(Csize):species, iter = iter, seed = seed,  
    RRPP = TRUE, SS.type = SS.type, effect.type = effect.type,  
    int.first = int.first, Cov = Cov, data = data, print.progress = print.progress)

This elucidates the issue.  There is no residual variation if species is in the model after accounting for phylogeny in estimation of model coefficients.  The reason the first attempt did not work is that in addition to the interaction, coefficients for both log(Csize) and species would be attempted first because SS.type = “I” was inherently implied, and there simply aren’t sufficient degrees of freedom to make estimation possible.  Sure enough, if we change the SS type, we can arrive at an answer.

> anova(procD.pgls(coords ~ log(Csize):species, data = df, phy = phy, SS.type = "III"))

Sums of Squares calculations: 1000 permutations.
  |==================================================================================| 100%

Analysis of Variance, using Residual Randomization
Permutation procedure: Randomization of null model residuals 
Number of permutations: 1000 
Estimation method: Generalized Least-Squares (via OLS projection) 
Sums of Squares and Cross-products: Type III 
Effect sizes (Z) based on F distributions
Df       SS   MS Rsq  F   Z Pr(>F)

log(Csize):species  8 0.043302    0   1  0 NaN  0.567
Residuals           0 0.000000 -Inf   0              
Total               8 0.043302                       

Call: procD.lm(f1 = coords ~ log(Csize):species, iter = iter, seed = seed,  
    RRPP = TRUE, SS.type = SS.type, effect.type = effect.type,  
    int.first = int.first, Cov = Cov, data = data, print.progress = print.progress)

This is not a good answer and is the same answer as before), but the analysis worked.  We could maybe have a better error message — if we had the foresight when one uses type I SS and a model that asks for species means after attempting to adjust estimation based on phylogenetic relatedness using the same species in the phylogeny — to explain the analysis was arrested because the user attempted something silly, but I hope you can appreciate that anticipating all illogical analyses is challenging.

The shorter response to your email could have been, “Don’t do that.” but I hope with this demonstration it is clear why you should not do that.

Best,
Mike

parts:
One little follow-up, because my explanation was not quite appropriate.  The invariance is not due solely or even in part because of the PGLS estimation, holding constant the effect of phylogeny.  The invariance is because as a factor, species has the same number of levels as observations in the data.  One could disregard the phylogeny and still have the same error.  For example:

> anova(procD.lm(coords ~ log(Csize) * species, data = df))

Error in (function (cond)  : 
  error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 'as.matrix': subscript out of bounds
> anova(procD.lm(coords ~ species, data = df))

Analysis of Variance, using Residual Randomization
Permutation procedure: Randomization of null model residuals 
Number of permutations: 1000
Estimation method: Ordinary Least Squares

Sums of Squares and Cross-products: Type I 
Effect sizes (Z) based on F distributions

          Df        SS         MS Rsq   F   Z Pr(>F)

species    8 0.0047685 0.00059607   1 NaN NaN  0.165
Residuals  0 0.0000000        NaN   0               
Total      8 0.0047685                              

Call: procD.lm(f1 = coords ~ species, data = df)

There is no replication if species is a term in the model, so there are no residuals.  Having extra model terms just makes the problem worse.

I apologize for any confusion.  I followed the example using PGLS and although I mentioned that degrees of freedom was an issue, I should not have implied that using PGLS was.  The same issue would persist irrespective of whether PGLS was used.

Mike

Dear Mike,
Thanks a lot for your detailed answer. Even though I'm a beginner, thanks to your explanation I could understand the source of the error.

Due to the fact that I can't address that aspect of my study with the procD.pgls function, I will be very grateful if you or any other member of this forum can suggest some alternatives.
Below I summarise some preliminary results of my analysis to try to outline my research.
1. Allometric with procD.lm shows interaction size:species and when comparing slopes showed heterogeneity
2. Phylogenetic signal (K: 1.3357, P-value: 0.026, Effect Size: 1.7104) with the physignal function
3. Phylomorphospace and PACA.

With the later analysis I already incorporate the phylogenetic signal. So, to complete my study I would like to include the assessment of allometry  "signal" taking into account the phylogeny.

Thanks in advance for any help!

Julio

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Error when I trying to assess evolutionary allometry with procD.pgls
parts:
Julio,

I apologize for not responding to this message earlier — geomorphR google group emails tend to go to my junk email box and if I don’t make a concerted effort to check it, I miss emails.

Are you suggesting for point #1 that your analysis was at the individual level and for #2 and #3 your analyses were at the species level (species means)?  If so, there is no really large problem.  What you have learned is that species tend to have divergent allometries, requiring allometry to be analyzed within-species.  There is no way to do a PGLS-type analysis that compares species means, accounting for allometry at a species level, based on disparate within-species allometries.  You can perform a species-level allometry analysis by finding species shape means and species size means, using these size means as a covariate in procD.pgls.  Just do not include species in your model.  But you would do this knowing that at the individual level, species have different allometries, so within- and among-species analyses are probably both needed.

Hope that helps.

Mike
